Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the wake-visual inspection skill, then trace the current rollout, inherited logs, and sampled results before changing exactly one candidate. The visual-signal skill will govern the required keyframe inspection before I touch the policy.

The contract confirms a single editable policy and forbids running CFD here. I’m inventorying the sampled successes/failures, inherited optimizer notes, and all available keyframe sheets now; I’ll anchor visual observations to the metric CSVs and diagnostics before writing the required pre-edit hypothesis.

The sampled evidence cleanly isolates the posterior acceleration ceiling: two exact 1700 runs and two exact 1650 runs. The 1650 pair improves arrival, distance, energy, and power again, while force/moment rise to 63.93/859.31; no sampled rollout is a semantic failure, so 1700 is the adverse finite comparator and the inherited 27° amplitude regression is the available failed hypothesis. I’m now inspecting the common prewarm and both distinct released sheets, as the skill requires.

The visual sheets confirm both ceilings use the same route: an initial target-facing turn, sustained left/down self-propulsion with a dense periodic trail, late entry into the merged wake, and clean target capture. At 1650, mean body velocity `(-0.3289,-0.1367)` remains distinct from local flow `(-0.1840,-0.1909)`, so the speedup is active rather than passive advection. I’ll record the required pre-edit diagnosis now, then make one isolated equal-step ceiling test; the current load growth will be an explicit rejection boundary, not treated as an unloading benefit.

The single solver change is now isolated to `posterior_acceleration_limit = 1600°/time²`; all propulsion, steering, observations, and parameter ownership remain unchanged. I’m revising the durable cap lesson because the newly sampled, exactly replicated 1650 result falsifies the parent’s earlier “stop at 1700” boundary, while simultaneously showing that load growth is steepening.

The required candidate notes and durable guidance are both updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s check-runner instructions now: first the parent-guidance semantic/schema guard, then the lightweight Julia policy call, then the editable-boundary check. These are contract checks only and do not run CFD.

The first check exposed a rendered-workspace issue before reaching my changes: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice, so the checker reports two “copied to guidance” markers. I’m inspecting the local checker and the duplicate lines to find the narrowest in-workspace repair, then I’ll rerun all checks.

The guidance check passes. The Julia contract command did not execute because this container has no `julia` on `PATH` (the preceding shell-profile SSH warnings are environmental), so I’m checking for a workspace-provided Julia binary before deciding whether that check is unavailable. No CFD was started.

The editable-boundary check passes, confirming only the permitted solver policy differs from the baseline. Since Julia is absent, I’m using the strongest available fallback: compare against the already evaluated 1650 policy to confirm the sole code delta is the numeric ceiling, and statically verify every `params.FIELD` use is declared by `target_policy_params()`.

A pinned Julia executable is available in the task runtime, so I can complete the prescribed lightweight contract check after all. I’m rerunning it with that binary; this remains a single policy function call, not a rollout.

All three prescribed checks now pass: material guidance/notes, lightweight Julia contract execution, and solver editable-boundary validation. I’m doing a final read-only handoff audit for exact file locations and confirming there is one assigned-parent marker and one solver delta.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:8), testing only a `1650 → 1600 deg/time²` posterior-acceleration ceiling step.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) with visual diagnosis, metrics, hypothesis, and rejection boundaries.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:122) with the replicated 1650 improvement and steepening load-cost lesson.
- Removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker from `README.md` that initially broke the required checker.

All required checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, parameter schema, and editable boundary. No CFD rollout was run.
